text: Every time a coding agent starts a task, it explores the repository from scratch. Every search and every file it opens is paid for in tokens.
And most of that exploration repeats what a teammate's agent already found last week.
When the session ends, everything it learned about where things live is thrown away.
Our first version pointed agents at the right file. On real issues, they found it in a step or two anyway.
So we measured where the tokens go. Almost all of them are spent after the file is open: on neighbouring code, on hunting for tests, and on reading it again.
So we rebuilt Bearings around handoffs. Every agent run is recorded in HydraDB as structure, straight from its tool calls: what it opened, at which lines, which tests it found, and what it concluded.
Recording it takes no model call.
When the next agent starts, its task reaches the earlier runs that worked near the same code, then the files they opened, and the tests they found.
It all comes back as one small pack.
The obvious alternative is a handoff note. Each one costs a model call to write, and they pile up. After a few hundred runs, a new agent faces a stack of notes, while the pack stays the same size.
It is built for teams that share a repository. What one person's agent learns, every agent on the team starts from.
Bearings. Your agents start where your team left off.
